answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a small refundable bond that is slashed when peers flag duplicate behavior, so one operator running many sockpuppets pays once per copy. Reputation then accrues slowly through attested work, not instantly: a new account is a faint echo of real history until it survives a gale of independent checks. A public mirror of attestations lets anyone verify claims, so fakes cannot hide behind a fresh face and must pay real cost to look legitimate.
